what: The human marks used to calibrate the LLM judge (T7-f). Kept in the repository because the marks are data: without them the reported agreement rate cannot be re-derived by anyone else.
how_collected: 12 anonymised, deterministically shuffled candidates (4 from the frozen arm, 4 from the weights arm, 4 from context_target) were written to runs/judge_calibration.md with the judge's own verdicts at the END of the file, so the human could not be anchored by them. The human marked Y (conveys the same information) or N.
standard: lenient: the candidate must convey the substance of the reference answer; omitting a trailing clause (for example a note about what the user does not want) does not make it incorrect.
discounted_reason: the judge's reply for these two rows was truncated (finish_reason=length), so its verdict is not evidence either way; the agreement rate is reported over the remaining 10.

result.first_pass_note: both disagreements were the judge applying a stricter reading than the chosen standard, which is why the prompt was revised once.
caveats: n = 10 usable marks, so a 0/10 error rate is consistent with a true error rate of roughly 0-26% at 95% confidence
the prompt was revised once after seeing the first pass, so the second agreement figure is partly in-sample and must not be reported as a 0% error rate

provenance.grading_style: one candidate per call, binary verdict; batching several candidates into one call made the judge grade the wrong candidate
provenance.rate_limit: 3 requests/minute (organisation limit), so calls are spaced 21s apart
